messages.subject: Multigroup Analysis
parts:
Hello Every one

I have a question for you, I appreciate your help.
I want to perform a multi group Analysis, I want to compare correlation between my Latent Variables among three countries and to show if these countries are showing different correlation coefficients. Here is my sample size for each country : France ~ 3000, Italy ~ 1000, Swiss ~ 500.
This is my question. Is it fair to perform a multi group analysis and conclude that whether or not the correlation coefficient is significantly changing among these countries?
In other words : to perform multi group analysis and show groups are different, is there any assumption about sample sizes ? should all groups have almost the same sample sizes or not? 
personally, I think it is not fair and groups should be equal, but on the other hand, I can see that Swiss is much smaller than France so I can not expect having the same sample size as France. I am not sure how to deal with it.
Thanks Every one.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Multigroup Analysis
parts: to perform multi group analysis and show groups are different, is there any assumption about sample sizes ? should all groups have almost the same sample sizes or not?

No assumption in the unrestricted model (freely estimate the correlation in each group).  If you fit a model constraining it to equality across groups, the estimate will be most driven by the largest group's data, because there is more of it.  But that doesn't cause a problem if you only use the restricted model to conduct a LRT of the equal-correlations null hypothesis (i.e., just don't interpret the "pooled estimate" as though it were actually an unweighted average across 3 countries).
personally, I think it is not fair and groups should be equal, but on the other hand, I can see that Swiss is much smaller than France so I can not expect having the same sample size as France.

If you want to interpret a pooled correlation from a constrained model, then it sounds like sampling weights should be used so that your results would reflect an average based on actual population sizes of those countries.
